newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Blue chips lead Seoul shares to a strong finish.
newsitem.headline: Blue chips lead Seoul shares to a strong finish.

text.p: South Korea's stocks ended Wednesday's trading on a strong note despite some late afternoon selling as domestic investors prepared for next week's foreign shareholdings limit expansion, brokers said.
The composite index ended 15.30 points higher to a provisional 793.21, after hitting a high of 798.46. Volume was an active 30.19 million shares.

"Samsung Electronics, POSCO and other blue chips that have been overlooked for a while, were in favour again because of the foreign ownership change on October 1," said Seoul Securities broker Park Hae-soo.
Foreigners will be able to buy up to 20 percent of most stocks from next Tuesday, against the current 18 percent.

Samsung Electronics, LG Electronics, and Pohang Iron and Steel were among those ending at their upper trading limits. Samsung gained 3,600 won to 63,800, LG rose 700 won to 14,000 and POSCO gained 2,500 won to 45,500.
Advancing shares beat decliners 622 to 240, while 121 were unchanged.
Brokers said some selling emerged as the index approached 800, which is seen as a strong resistance level.

Individual shares backed by themes also saw active buying. Asset-rich Young Poong Mining was the most active share of the day, rising 3,500 won to 66,000. Banks and securities firms gained on speculation that the sector will be hit with takeovers next year when the government eases M&A regulations.
The December futures contract rose 2.30 points to 84.80, while the KOSPI 200 index gained 2.02 points to 83.12.
The market will be closed for the Korean Thanksgiving holidays from September 26 to 28 and will resume next week.
